title: Same seed, same game
description:
A random engine started from the same **seed** always produces the same sequence. Games use this for replays, and tests use it to get repeatable results.

Read a seed and a number of rolls. Seed a `std::mt19937` with that seed, roll a six-sided die that many times, and print the rolls on one line separated by spaces, then how many sixes there were:

```
Rolls: 1 5 2 6 4
Sixes: 1
```

(The exact numbers depend on the seed.) To match the expected output, create **one** engine, **one** `std::uniform_int_distribution<int>{ 1, 6 }`, and call it exactly once per roll.
hints: Store each roll in a variable before using it. Calling `die(rng)` twice for one roll (once to print, once to test) would use up two random numbers.
